extracted.intended_audience: Program Directors/Principal Investigators (PD/PIs), Authorized Organization Representatives (AORs), and institutional officials involved in NIH grant applications and appeals
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural guidance for submitting and processing appeals of NIH initial scientific peer review outcomes, including eligibility, allowable grounds, submission requirements, timelines, Council review, withdrawal, and outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may file an appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal is a written communication from a Program Director/Principal Investigator (PD/PI) and/or applicant institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The applicant organization may designate multiple PD/PIs; each PD/PI remains responsible and accountable. The appeal must display concurrence from the Authorized Organization Representative (AOR).

rubrics_metrics.name: AOR concurrence requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal letter must display concurrence from the Authorized Organization Representative (AOR) of the applicant organization for the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although content may originate from the PD/PI or organizational officials, the AOR must send the letter directly to the Program Official (PO), or must send their concurrence to the PD/PI who will forward the materials and AOR concurrence to the PO. A communication from the PD/PI or institutional official (other than the AOR) only or with a 'cc' to the AOR will not be accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for filing an appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal must be received after issuance of the summary statement and up to 30 calendar days after the second level of peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the appeal letter was received by the IC deadline, the PD/PI and AOR will receive a written explanation of the resolution no later than 30 calendar days after the Council meeting. If received after the IC deadline, the Executive Secretary will provide, no more than 30 calendar days after receipt, a written explanation of the IC's plan for making the appeal available to Council.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content requirements of the appeal letter
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal letter will be accepted only if it (1) describes the flaws in the review process for the application in question, (2) explains the reasons for the appeal, and (3) is based on one or more allowable issues related to the process of the initial peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PO will send the PD/PI and/or institutional official, and AOR, an acknowledgement letter within 10 days of receipt of the appeal letter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable issue: evidence of bias
rubrics_metrics.description: One allowable basis for appeal is evidence of bias on the part of one or more peer reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeal must describe specific evidence of reviewer bias as the procedural flaw; general complaints without specifics are unlikely to meet the standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable issue: conflict of interest (42 CFR Part 52h.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal may be based on conflict of interest, as specified in regulation at 42 CFR Part 52h.5 'Scientific Peer Review of Research Grant Applications and Research and Development Contract Projects', on the part of one or more non-Federal peer reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allegations should reference the regulation and explain how the conflict affected the review process or outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable issue: lack of appropriate expertise in the SRG
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal may be based on a lack of appropriate expertise within the Scientific Review Group (SRG).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe how missing or inappropriate expertise in the SRG constituted a procedural flaw affecting evaluation of the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable issue: factual errors by reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal may be based on factual error(s) made by one or more reviewers that could have altered the outcome of review substantially.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify the factual error(s) and explain why correction of those errors would likely have changed the review outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific opinion differences are not appealable
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeal letters based solely on differences of scientific opinion will not be accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an explicit anti-pattern: disagreements about scientific interpretation or judgment do not constitute procedural flaws for appeal purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission route and acknowledgement
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal letter must be submitted, either in hard copy or electronically, to the Program Official (PO).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PO will send an acknowledgement letter within 10 days of receipt. The AOR must send concurrence directly to the PO or send concurrence to the PD/PI for forwarding; improper routing (PD/PI-only or cc to AOR) will not be accepted as meeting the AOR requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusions and inapplicability of the appeal policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The NIH policy for appeals of initial peer review does not apply to appeals of the technical evaluation of Research and Development contract projects, appeals of NIH funding decisions, or appeals of decisions concerning extensions of MERIT awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As stated in the Notice of Funding Opportunity, appeals of initial peer review outcome will not be accepted for applications in response to an RFA. NIH will not review a resubmission application when an appeal of initial peer review is pending on the original application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper or deficient letters treated as grievances
rubrics_metrics.description: A letter that does not meet appeal criteria and/or does not include the concurrence of the AOR will not be considered an appeal letter, but rather a grievance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grievances are handled according to IC-specific procedures; applicants should contact the IC for guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of an appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: If review staff and program staff do not support the appeal, or do not agree on its merit, the PD/PI and/or an institutional official may elect to withdraw the appeal letter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The request to withdraw must be submitted to the PO, display concurrence from the AOR, and follow the same AOR routing rules as the original appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral to Council if unresolved
rubrics_metrics.description: If review staff and program staff do not support the appeal, or do not agree on its merit, and the appeal letter is not withdrawn, the appeal letter will be made available to Council.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The IC may not deny the PD/PI or applicant organization the opportunity to have an appeal letter made available to Council.

rubrics_metrics.name: Possible Council outcomes and finality
rubrics_metrics.description: Only two outcomes are possible following consideration of an appeal letter by Council: (1) Council may concur with the appeal and recommend that the application be re-reviewed; or (2) Council may concur with the SRG's recommendation and deny the appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although factual errors or other issues may be evident, Council may determine these factors were unlikely to alter the final outcome and deny the appeal. No action by Council is equivalent to concurrence with the SRG's recommendation and denial of the appeal. The recommendation of Council concerning resolution of an appeal is final and will not be considered again by the NIH through this or another process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-review rules if Council recommends re-review
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Council recommended that the application be re-reviewed, the original application will be re-reviewed without additional materials or modifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The application may be re-reviewed by the same or a different SRG depending on the flaws in the original review process. In most cases, re-review will entail re-assignment to a subsequent review round and delay in the final funding decision. The outcome of the re-review is final and cannot be appealed again.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication of Council recommendation and timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: The Executive Secretary for the Council will communicate the Council recommendation concerning an appeal to the PD/PI, AOR, and NIH staff with a need to know.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the appeal letter was received by the IC deadline, PD/PI and AOR will receive a written explanation no later than 30 calendar days after the Council meeting. If received after the IC deadline, the Executive Secretary will provide, within 30 calendar days after receipt, a written explanation of the IC's plan for making the appeal available to Council.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH may suspend the appeals policy temporarily
rubrics_metrics.description: On occasion, and for specific circumstances, the NIH may suspend temporarily the policy and process for handling appeals of NIH initial peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such decisions will be announced in NIH Guide Notices and/or the relevant Notice of Funding Opportunity.
